correctness.rationale: Rank-one closed syntax decomposes into existential/universal one-variable quantifier-free clauses and Boolean outer connectives. Downward closure and singleton supplementation prove necessity under support-preserving thinning. Repeated constancy splitting defines each unary-colour count upper bound; Dickson minimal forbidden vectors prove the converse. A capacity induction (literal capacities 0/infinity, constancy 1, conjunction min, split disjunction sum) proves the pure-equality cost exactly. Explicit finite semantic checker reproduced all four declared test batteries. No finite test is used to justify an infinite quantifier.

value.rationale: This is a complete and natural classification of finite monadic properties at the smallest positive dependence-logic quantifier rank, including explicit forbidden-basis normal forms and an optimal occurrence lower bound. It separates the expressiveness of depth one from its potentially arbitrarily large formula size, and identifies the first rank barrier against positive cardinality thresholds, motivating future semantic and finite-model investigations. It does not rely merely on an arbitrary small numerical improvement.
